item.text:
Research continuation completed across all eight chapters. No scores or judge recommendations were produced.

The shell remained unavailable due to the sandbox network-namespace failure, so I could not persist `research-materials.md` or `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The following ledger-ready additions and disposition changes should be applied by the parent process.

### 1B — Nuclear and existential risk

- **N072 — IAEA safeguards status** — The IAEA country factsheet records Nigeria’s NPT safeguards agreement in force from 1988 and Additional Protocol signed in 2001/in force from 2007. This is target-period institutional context, not evidence of Tinubu’s personal restraint. Contrary limitation: safeguards status does not prove absence of dual-use, radiological, biological, or other catastrophic-risk capability. Disposition: `final_evidence`, bounded to safeguards status. Links: 1B.1, 1B.3, 1B.4, 1B.10. [IAEA country factsheet](https://ola.iaea.org/Applications/FactSheets/Country/Detail?code=NG)

Shortfall remains substantial: no authoritative source establishing complete non-possession or a Tinubu-attributable 2023 CBRN decision was recovered. The prior Wikipedia item remains `discovery_only`/context, not final evidence.

### 2B — International peace, restraint, and lawful security

- **N073 — ECOWAS Niger communiqué** — The 30 July 2023 communiqué condemned the coup, demanded restoration of constitutional order, imposed financial/travel measures, and authorized further measures if demands were unmet. It also recognized Tinubu’s ECOWAS chairmanship. Attribution is collective and must not be treated as solely personal. Contrary: diplomacy and an envoy were also mandated; Nigeria did not invade Niger in 2023. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [ECOWAS communiqué](https://ecowas.int/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Final-Communique_Extra-Summit-on-Niger.pdf)

- **N074 — Tinubu’s dialogue position** — The State House reported Tinubu describing dialogue and negotiation as the “bedrock” of the Niger response and citing mediation teams and envoys. Contrary: this coexisted with sanctions and possible-force authorization. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [State House report](https://statehouse.gov.ng/niger-republic-at-2nd-ecowas-extraordinary-summit-president-tinubu-champions-dialogue-to-resolve-impasse/)

- **N075 — Envoy to Niamey** — Tinubu dispatched a delegation led by Abdulsalami Abubakar to negotiate with Niger’s coup leaders. The mission did not restore constitutional rule during 2023. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [State House report](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-dispatches-envoy-to-niamey-urges-robust-dialogue-to-end-impasse/)

This chapter now has a defensible primary-record lane covering coercion, diplomacy, and non-intervention. Remaining shortfall: no complete audit of arms transfers, proxies, cross-border operations, or other foreign-policy theaters.

### 3B — Domestic safety and protection

- **N076 — Tudun Biri airstrikes** — Amnesty reported two Nigerian military airstrikes on 3 December 2023 against a religious gathering, killing more than 120 civilians, with contradictory military explanations and alleged mass graves. Attribution is directly relevant to the federal commander-in-chief, while operational responsibility remains institutional. Tinubu’s condolences and investigation order are mitigating but do not erase the civilian-harm evidence. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [Amnesty International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/12/nigeria-military-attempting-to-cover-up-mass-killing-of-civilians/)

- **N077 — Six-month human-rights assessment** — Amnesty reported continuing excessive force, extrajudicial killings, arbitrary detention, torture, unresolved counterinsurgency abuses, and lack of remedy during Tinubu’s first six months. This supports institutional responsibility and accountability concerns, not proof of a presidential order or knowledge. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [Amnesty International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/press-release/2023/11/after-six-months-in-office-nigerian-president-tinubu-has-failed-to-uphold-human-rights/)

- **N078 — Labour protest assault** — Contemporary reporting records police beating and blindfolding NLC president Joe Ajaero during a 1 November 2023 Imo protest. Police disputed the characterization, saying he was taken into protective custody. Presidential responsibility is indirect and unresolved. Disposition: `final_evidence`, attribution caveat. [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/c2d1e48e280037e178d6703cd9ac7cd4)

The protest-treatment gap is materially improved. Remaining shortfall: no complete target-period emergency-powers, surveillance, or security-force accountability audit.

### 4B — Political freedom and authoritarian restraint

- **N079 — Freedom House internet-freedom assessment** — The 2023 country report records persistent online self-censorship, surveillance concerns, opaque content restrictions, and cybercrime-law risks. Much of the underlying history predates Tinubu’s inauguration, so this is primarily context. Disposition: `context`. [Freedom House](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2023)

- **N080 — Election-period connectivity** — Access Now’s 2023 election monitoring reported Nigeria’s commitment to maintain internet access and no election-related shutdown. Attribution is governmental and limited; it does not establish later digital restraint. Disposition: `final_evidence`, limited attribution.

- **N081 — Amnesty media-freedom finding** — Amnesty reported that at least 42 journalists were attacked, harassed, beaten, or denied access during the 2023 elections, and that expression and media freedom remained routinely violated. This is target-year rights evidence, but the responsible-agent chain is mixed. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [Amnesty International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/press-release/2023/11/after-six-months-in-office-nigerian-president-tinubu-has-failed-to-uphold-human-rights/)

Remaining shortfall: direct presidential nexus for press incidents, post-election opposition treatment, and executive influence over courts/oversight.

### 5B — Economic well-being

- **N082 — December inflation** — NBS recorded headline inflation of 28.92% in December 2023, up from 21.34% in December 2022; month-on-month inflation was 2.29%. Food inflation reached 33.93%. Attribution is shared between inherited conditions and Tinubu-era reforms. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [NBS CPI report](https://www.nigerianstat.gov.ng/elibrary/read/1241439)

- **N083 — World Bank reform effects** — The December Nigeria Development Update reported gasoline prices up approximately 163%, official naira depreciation around 41%, parallel-market depreciation around 30%, and inflation partly driven by subsidy removal. It characterized the reforms as potentially necessary but painful and incomplete. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/12/13/turning-the-corner-time-to-move-from-reforms-to-results)

- **N084 — Cash-transfer implementation** — The World Bank presentation records a ₦25,000 monthly transfer for three months, launched 17 October 2023; 1.5 million households had reportedly received money, with five million expected by year-end. This establishes partial delivery, not full reach or effectiveness. Disposition: `final_evidence`, delivery caveat. [World Bank presentation](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/88d5ed4248d7063eced528070a83173e-0360012023/original/NDU-december-2023-presentation.pdf)

The chapter now has direct target-period macro outcomes and partial mitigation evidence. Remaining shortfall: verified subsidy savings, actual reinvestment, FX outcomes beyond aggregate depreciation, and correction after adverse effects.

### 6B — Social well-being and human development

- **N085 — WHO health delivery outcomes** — WHO reports 2022–23 Nigeria outcomes including 94% HIV-status awareness, 100% ART coverage among identified patients, 93% viral suppression, a 59% increase in TB notification, improved TB treatment coverage, and large vaccination reach. Attribution is shared with pre-existing programs and partners, not solely Tinubu. Disposition: `final_evidence`, shared-attribution caveat. [WHO Nigeria profile](https://www.who.int/about/accountability/results/who-results-report-2022-2023/country-profile/2023/nigeria)

- **N086 — Welfare shock and response** — The World Bank reports that inflation and reform-related price increases were especially harmful to poor and vulnerable households, while targeted transfers were intended to cushion the shock. Disposition: `final_evidence`, outcome/intent separated. [World Bank Nigeria Development Update](https://www.worldbank.org/en/country/nigeria/publication/nigeria-development-update-ndu)

- **N087 — Labour cost-of-living strike** — AP reports a September 2023 NLC warning strike over rising costs after subsidy removal, with workers describing “mass suffering” and inadequate government relief. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/c2d1e48e280037e178d6703cd9ac7cd4)

The chapter is no longer empty. Remaining shortfall: education delivery, full-year poverty and household-income measures, and verified beneficiary reach for relief programs.

### 7B — Personal integrity and honesty

- The Bawa material should be **split and retained** as follows:
  - **N088 — Official suspension record** — Channels TV records Tinubu’s indefinite suspension of EFCC chair AbdulRasheed Bawa to permit investigation into allegations of abuse of office. Disposition: `final_evidence`.
  - **N089 — Independent corroboration** — Al Jazeera independently corroborates the suspension and EFCC’s anti-corruption mandate. Disposition: `final_evidence`, but do not infer that the action obstructed an investigation into Tinubu without a direct record.

- **N090 — Asset-declaration requirement** — The CCB required incoming officials to file asset declarations before inauguration. No public copy or compliance verification for Tinubu was recovered. Disposition: `context`/unresolved gap. [CCB asset declaration information](https://ccb.gov.ng/?page_id=325)

The strongest unresolved integrity question remains whether Bawa’s suspension obstructed a Tinubu-related investigation. No direct case file, asset declaration, or verified personal-finance record was recovered.

### 8B — Effectiveness and competence

- **N091 — Budget implementation archive** — The Budget Office maintains first- through fourth-quarter 2023 implementation reports. This is a recoverable primary route, but the reports were not extracted sufficiently here. Disposition: `discovery_only`. [Budget Office archive](https://budgetoffice.gov.ng/index.php/resources/internal-resources/reports/quarterly-budget-implementation/2023-budget-implementation-reports)

- **N092 — Supplementary-budget decision** — The National Assembly record documents Tinubu’s submission of a ₦2.8 trillion supplementary appropriation for infrastructure and subsidy palliatives. It establishes an adaptation decision and legislative process, not execution or delivery. Disposition: `final_evidence`. [National Assembly](https://nass.gov.ng/news/item/1716)

- **N093 — Spending-priority contrary evidence** — AP reports that the 2023 supplementary budget included approximately $38 million for presidential and vice-presidential vehicles, aircraft, and residential renovations amid severe household hardship. This is relevant to prioritization and distribution, but not proof of personal enrichment. Disposition: `final_evidence`, bounded to budget priorities. [Associated Press](https://apnews.com/article/nigeria-tinubu-budget-yacht-suvs-8bfd1d6c7e6838d17d9c5dd33ec92a4f)

Effectiveness evidence now includes target-period reform outcomes, mitigation, and a contrary spending-priority record. Remaining shortfall: actual budget execution, delivery milestones, coordination, adaptation, and year-end security outcomes.

### Manifest instructions

Preserve all prior usable evidence. Add N072–N093 with the dispositions above. Demote or retain as follows:

- Wikipedia-derived exposure and event summaries: `context` or `discovery_only` unless independently corroborated.
- Post-2023 retrospective items: `context`, never target-period final evidence.
- Budget Office archive: `discovery_only` until PDFs are opened and extracted.
- Country-level V-Dem, Freedom House, corruption, and capacity measures: `context` unless the ledger field is explicitly a country-year baseline rather than ruler conduct.
- Do not retain the prior researcher conclusions recommending scores, nulls, or exposure classifications.

The eight chapters remain research-incomplete, with the largest remaining recoverable tasks in 1B exposure completeness, 2B non-Niger foreign-policy coverage, 3B accountability/emergency powers, 4B opposition and digital controls, 5B realized savings and correction, 6B education and welfare reach, 7B asset/investigation records, and 8B budget execution.
